sample_unit: psychiatric clinical notes (over 1,000, segmented into sequential stages)

links.outcome: LLM under-abstention and over-abstention when clinical information is incomplete (DIAGNOSE/CLARIFY/ABSTAIN)
links.effect: Under-abstention exceeded 60% for most models; safety-aware prompting reduced premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention; models rarely sought clarification unless explicitly prompted.
links.quote: Our findings show that capability does not ensure calibration: even strong models struggle under incomplete clinical information, with under-abstention exceeding 60% for most models and safety-aware prompting reducing premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention.

screen.reason: The study develops a benchmark (Safe-Psych) evaluating sequential diagnostic uncertainty in psychiatry and tests safety-aware prompting strategies to evaluate their effect on premature commitment and abstention/clarification behaviors.

primary.practice: safety-aware prompting for abstention and clarification
